requirements.evidence: Contract items are all present: action signature (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:21`), Queue fillable/casts/relations (`app/Models/Queue.php:12-39`), Ticket casts/nextCode/call (`app/Models/Ticket.php:14-112`), enums, exception, Entity::queues (`app/Models/Entity.php:46-49`) and both migrations (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_041300_create_queues_table.php:14-23`, `database/migrations/2026_10_29_041301_create_tickets_table.php:14-27`); the >999, deleted-number, malformed-code and stale/inactive-queue cases are handled and tested. `call()` is not atomic (`app/Models/Ticket.php:97-112`) and the next-code lookup scans every code (`app/Models/Ticket.php:82-86`), so it is strong but not a clean 5.

conventions.evidence: Domain write is an invokable action (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:14-55`), migrations are generator-style with reversible `down()` (`database/migrations/2026_10_29_041300_create_queues_table.php:30-33`), fillable is deliberate (`app/Models/Queue.php:12`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:14`), Pest tests ship with the change, and both required docs plus `CHANGELOG.md:12` are updated (`docs/business-rules.md:67-94`, `docs/database-schema.md:147-161`). Deviation: `Ticket::call()` does a raw membership lookup instead of a policy/gate (`app/Models/Ticket.php:103-107`).

security.evidence: The only new write path authorizes before mutating and throws `AuthorizationException` (`app/Models/Ticket.php:103-107`); issuance validates priority before any write (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:23-25`); there is no HTTP/Livewire input, no rendered output, no secret handling, and the fillable lists are limited to domain fields (`app/Models/Queue.php:12`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:14`). No exploitable weakness found.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: defaults, priority/channel, >999, deleted numbers, malformed codes, inactive/stale queue and negative priority (`tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:13-96`); schema, indexes, cascades, factories and relations (`tests/Feature/Queue/QueueTicketSchemaTest.php:13-104`); call, double-call, non-member and write-once (`tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCallTest.php:28-68`). The required collision-retry path has no test, and the non-member test only uses a user with no membership anywhere.

simplicity.evidence: One small action reuses Eloquent and factories rather than adding layers; but `IssueTicket` contains a dead catch (`app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:47-48`) and `nextCode()` loads every code per issuance with an `orderBy('id')` that the max loop ignores (`app/Models/Ticket.php:82-86`).

readability.evidence: Names and methods are focused (`IssueTicket::__invoke`, `Ticket::nextCode`, `Ticket::call`) and comments explain the non-obvious rules (`app/Models/Ticket.php:43-54`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:74-77`). Minor style slips: fully-qualified `LogicException` in a file that imports its other classes (`app/Models/Ticket.php:57`, `app/Models/Ticket.php:100`) and a global `memberOf()` helper (`tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCallTest.php:13-26`).

scope.evidence: Every file maps to the task: two migrations, Queue/Ticket models plus Entity::queues, two enums, the exception, the action, two factories, three test files, the two required docs and the CHANGELOG entry. Call-next selection, queue UI and the totem API are untouched.

issues.explanation: `call()` refreshes, checks `waiting`, then saves in a separate statement with no transaction or conditional update, so two concurrent callers can both pass and the later one overwrites `called_by_user_id`, breaking the "exactly once" rule.
No test forces a duplicate `(queue_id, code)` to exercise the `QueryException` retry loop required by the task, so the retry behavior is unverified.
The unauthorized test uses a user with no membership anywhere; it does not cover a user who belongs to a different entity, so the entity scoping of `membershipFor()` is not actually proven.
Authorization is a raw `membershipFor()` lookup inside the model rather than the project's policy/gate pattern, bypassing the central authorization layer.
`catch (InactiveQueueException) { throw $e; }` is dead code: an `InactiveQueueException` is not a `QueryException`, so it would propagate past the following catch even without this block.
`orderBy('id')` is wasted because the loop keeps the numeric maximum, and the method loads every code for the queue on each issuance; a last-row or counter query would be leaner.

The status check runs before the membership check, so a non-member calling an already-called ticket gets `LogicException` instead of the specified `AuthorizationException` and can infer the ticket's state.
The "Unique constraints" note still says `tickets (queue_id, code)` is unique "per issuance window", contradicting the migration's permanent per-queue unique index and the updated code notes.
Minor style slips: fully-qualified `LogicException` in a file that imports its other classes, and a global `memberOf()` test helper that could collide with another Pest file.

review.summary: Adds the queue/ticket persistence, models, enums, exception, factories and the invokable `IssueTicket` action with a locked inactive-queue re-read, collision retry, write-once guard and single authorized call, plus the required docs, CHANGELOG and broad Pest coverage. The implementation is in good shape and I would approve it with minor changes: `call()` is not atomic, the retry path is untested, and there is a dead catch and a small doc inconsistency. Confidence is medium because this directory has no composer.json to confirm the Laravel version needed for `#[Fillable]`/`Schema::hasIndex` and no existing `User` model to confirm `membershipFor()`.
